newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INTERVIEW - Enseval says to focus on core.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Enseval says to focus on core.

text.p: PT Enseval Putra Megatrading, one of Indonesia's largest trading firms, said on Thursday it had reduced its stake in photo equipment distributor Inter Delta to focus on distributing pharmaceutical products.

"We have reduced our stake in Inter Delta last week to 15.04 percent from the previous 30.04 percent as part of our efforts to focus more on our core business and boost earnings," Enseval managing director Krishnan Sjarif told Reuters.
Sjarif declined to say whether the firm was planning to further reduce its stake in Inter Delta, saying it had to discuss the matter with its holding company, the Kalbe Group.
He also declined to reveal the buyer, but said the sale involved around 2.3 million shares worth some 3.4 billion rupiah which would be used to repay loans.
Inter Delta distributes Eastman Kodak photographic equipment and office equipment from Japan's Canon and Noritsu Koki.

Enseval distributes various pharmaceutical products, consumer health care products and medical equipment from around 50 local and foreign principals including Kalbe Farma, Bristol-Myers Squibb Indonesia and Pfizer, he said.
Sjarif said Enseval was also in final negotiations with a large foreign firm to set up a joint venture.
"The negotiation is still going on, but it has reached the final stage. The only major issue is that both sides would like to become the majority shareholder," Sjarif said.
He said a memorandum of understanding was expected to be signed later this year.
Sjarif declined to name the foreign partner and to elaborate on the financial impact of the venture on Enseval.
"The new firm is expected to better manage our existing distribution facilities for example by offering them not just for our principals but also for others," he said.
He declined to say the investment amount involved in the new firm, but said it was likely to be relatively low.
Sjarif said sales from pharmaceutical products formed the largest contribution to total sales last year and was expected to remain the firm's core business in the coming years.

"Around 62 percent of the total sales last year came from the distribution of pharmaceutical products, 25 percent from consumer products, three to four percent from the distribution of medical equipment and the rest from raw pharmaceutical material," Sjarif said.
He said the firm expected total sales growth to remain at around 15 percent this year in line with the 15-18 percent growth of the national pharmaceutical industry.
Enseval posted net sales of 572.59 billion rupiah in 1995 against 499.06 billion rupiah in 1994.
It expected a net profit of 18 billion rupiah in 1996 against 15.71 billion rupiah in 1995, Syarif said.
